content_metadata.description: An educational video that explores the sources and impact of wastewater, including real-world consequences of water pollution and solutions such as water treatment and conservation.

qAndA.question: What color is the water droplet that acts as the narrator?

qAndA.answer: Waterborne disease, the teacher states that is the general term for it. However, he mentions typhoid.
qAndA.question: What waterborne disease did Sunil suffer from?

qAndA.answer: Bathing (lather and dirt) and washing utensils (food particles, soap).
qAndA.question: What are two sources of wastewater, as mentioned in the video?

qAndA.answer: Manholes provide access points for inspecting and maintaining sewer pipes where two or more sewers converge.
qAndA.question: Why are manholes necessary in sewage systems?

qAndA.answer: The teacher emphasizes the scarcity of clean water and highlights the benefits of treating and reusing wastewater. This message is reinforced by the concerned mood of the students when they discuss the health impacts of water pollution.
qAndA.question: How does the video convey the importance of water conservation?

scenes.title: Introduction

activities.description: Rakesh greets Sunil and asks about his absence.
Sunil explains he was sick with fever and vomiting.
Sunil explains the doctor said it was due to water pollution.
The teacher enters the classroom.
The teacher asks about Sunil's health.
Sunil responds that he is better.
The teacher asks how water makes people sick.

characterInteraction.description: Rakesh and Sunil engage in a friendly conversation.
The teacher interacts with Sunil and the class, asking questions about waterborne diseases.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Transition to curious as students welcome the teacher

scenes.thematicElements: Waterborne diseases, Health impact of water pollution
scenes.title: Classroom Dialogue 1

videoEditingDetails.description: Thought bubble appears showing Sunil sick in bed
Thought bubbles appear showing a doctor and industrial pollution

activities.description: The teacher asks how water gets dirty.
A girl responds, stating water gets dirty from bathing.
The teacher confirms and defines wastewater.
Another girl explains wastewater also comes from various household activities.
The teacher introduces the concept of sewers.
The teacher asks if they've seen pipes at home.
Students affirm seeing pipes.
The teacher explains the purpose of sewers and manholes.
A girl asks if muddy water causes water pollution when mixed with clean water and inquires about its destination.
The teacher confirms and explains the consequences of poor sewage systems and the importance of water treatment.
Sunil expresses concern about getting sick from reused water.
A girl asks what can be done with wastewater.
The teacher explains the need for treating wastewater to prevent pollution and waterborne diseases.
Rakesh asks if dirty water can be purified.
The teacher explains the role of water treatment plants.
Sunil asks if reusing treated water is safe.
The teacher clarifies that treated wastewater is safe for reuse and emphasizes the importance of water conservation.

characterInteraction.description: The teacher and students engage in active dialogue throughout the scene.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Transition to hopeful as the teacher explains solutions for treating water

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Waste Water Story Part 1
Hello kids, you have seen in the video on water as to how essential water is for us.
If there is water, there is life.
Water is very important.
Not only for humans, but also for animals, birds and plants.
Due to increasing population, increasing industrialization, expansion in agriculture, increasing
urbanization, the water level is decreasing.
Is the water that is available for us clean and useful?
In this video, we will learn about waste water and other aspects related to it.
To know more on this subject, we take you to a village in Hariana.
The objective of this video is to understand what is waste water.
Hey Sunil, long time, wherever you all these days, you look very tired and sick.
Yes, my friend, I was sick.
I had fever and vomiting.
Oh, is it?
Doctor told me that I had fever due to water pollution.
Hmm, look, sir has come to the class.
Good morning, sir.
Hello children, Sunil, how are you?
I am fine, sir.
I was ill.
The doctor said that I had a water-borne disease.
Children, can you tell us how we get sick due to water?
Sir, when water is polluted, then we get water-borne diseases.
Correct.
People get sick due to waste water or dirty water.
We will first learn what is waste water.
Can anyone tell me how the water gets dirty?
Sir, when we bathe and the water is filled with water, it becomes dirty water.
Correct.
Domestic water and the water that is generated after commercial use is called waste water
or dirty water.
The water that comes out from washing utensils, from bathing, washing of hands, washing
of clothes etc is also dirty water.
Yes, this water contains vegetable matter.
Oil used in food, hair oil, detergent, floor dust, lubricated soapy water after washing
the human body.
This water is called grey water.
Sir, there is water that we used in the toilets too.
Right.
The water released from flushing the human excretor and to wash is called black water or sewage.
Children, when it rains or the drain is filled, you see that the water flows on the road.
Observe this water.
Try to color, smell or any other observation of this flowing water and discuss it with
your teacher.
All this water goes into the drains, isn't it, sir?
Have you seen small and big pipes at your homes?
Yes, we saw them.
Pipes that carry dirty water are called sewers.
One pipe is for good water management in our houses and other pipes bring out the dirty
water from the house.
Every 50 to 60 meters, there are manholes where two or more sewers are found.
Sir, this muddy water causes water pollution when mixed with clean water.
Where does this water go?
If there is no good sewerage system, dirty water contaminates clean water and also becomes
a factor for many fatal diseases.
Old pipes, leakage in sewerage system, industrial waste and human excretor directly going into
the lakes and rivers pollutes the water.
Many germs thrive in this contaminated water and cause various diseases.
The germs carrying typhoid, hepatitis, cholera, diarrhea, dysentery, skin diseases etc.
Thrive in such contaminated water.
Oh, I feel sick due to this.
Sir, then what can we do with the waste water?
We should not let the dirty water go waste.
By removing contaminants from it, it can be made clean and reused again.
Can so much dirty water be purified?
Yes, dirty water is sanitized with the help of a water treatment plant.
But why, sir?
Will we not get sick from reusing this water?
Due to the continuous scarcity of clean water, the dirty water is cleaned and reused.
If we do not treat sewer generated in large quantities, this muddy water will pollute lakes,
rivers and ground water without interruption.
Therefore, water must be treated.
How is this treatment done, sir?
I will tell you about it tomorrow.
It is now time.
Remember, water is precious and we should understand the value of safe drinking water.
Therefore, we should not waste water.
Water should be used with caution.
One should not waste be used with caution.
Rakesh is right. See you tomorrow.
Thank you, sir.
Children, in this video you have learnt about waste water and its different aspects.
Many diseases are spread due to water pollution.
That is why dirty water should not be mixed with clean water.
In the next video, you will learn about the process of cleaning waste water.
See you.
Thank you.
